answer: Spectral Cutoff uses neighbor-set overlap: an identity is admitted only if its declared peers share at least k of its own neighbors, measured over rolling epochs. Isolated clusters get their relay capacity throttled to a juniper minimum, so fake swarms cannot route or trade. Honest agents earn nectar-weighted placement by holding stable, cross-linked edges. Attackers must sustain real bidirectional traffic across many distinct nodes per identity, paying bandwidth and latency umber overhead that scales with fleet size.
